topic: first irrigation timing after sowing crown root initiation
text: The first post-sowing irrigation in wheat is timed at crown root initiation, about 20 to 25 days after sowing. Punjab Agricultural University lists it as the first of its recommended post-sowing irrigations.
source_title: Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 90(3), 2020: sowing dates, planting methods and irrigation treatments in wheat (PAU, Ludhiana)

topic: irrigation schedule stages tillering jointing booting milking
text: Punjab Agricultural University's recommended four post-sowing irrigations for wheat are at crown root initiation (20 to 25 days after sowing), tillering (40 to 45 days), jointing or booting (60 to 70 days) and milking (100 to 105 days). A three-irrigation schedule tested in the same study used crown root initiation, flag leaf emergence (70 to 80 days) and soft dough (115 to 120 days).
source_title: Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 90(3), 2020: sowing dates, planting methods and irrigation treatments in wheat (PAU, Ludhiana)

topic: crown root initiation importance first irrigation weeks
text: Crown root initiation is treated as the most important stage for irrigating wheat because of its role in root development and nutrient availability. A department of agriculture guide from Sindh, Pakistan gives the first wheat irrigation as 3 to 4 weeks after sowing, which is consistent with the 20 to 25 day figure from Indian Punjab studies.
source_title: Agriculture Department, Government of Sindh: irrigation scheduling guide (Pakistan)

topic: first irrigation depth amount of water mm
text: In Punjab Agricultural University field and simulation studies on irrigation scheduling, wheat grain yield rose significantly when the first irrigation was increased from 65 mm to 75 mm of water. Going further to 85 mm gave only a small numerical gain. These were research results for irrigated wheat, so actual quantities should be confirmed with the local KVK.
source_title: Optimizing irrigation schedule for wheat through field and simulation studies (PAU thesis, KrishiKosh)

topic: nitrogen urea fertilizer split application timing sowing first irrigation
text: In a sowing-time trial in Punjab, applying half of the nitrogen at sowing and half at the first irrigation gave wheat yield on par with a three-way split (half at sowing, a quarter at the first irrigation and a quarter at the second) and significantly better than the other timings tested. The total dose should follow the Soil Health Card or the local KVK.
source_title: Indian Journal of Agronomy: sowing time and split nitrogen in bread wheat (Amritsar, Punjab)

topic: urea nitrogen top dressing before or after irrigation timing
text: A Journal of Wheat Research study for the wheat belt of Haryana and Punjab found that top dressing urea just before irrigation improved wheat growth compared with top dressing it after irrigation.
source_title: Journal of Wheat Research: nitrogen top dressing just before irrigation improves wheat growth

topic: weed control weeding critical period hand weeding days after sowing
text: A Tamil Nadu Agricultural University guide puts the critical period of weed control in wheat at 15 to 30 days after sowing. Where no herbicide is used it advises two hand weedings, at about 20 and 35 days after sowing. This guide is from another state, so local advice should be confirmed with the KVK.
source_title: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University agritech portal: weed management in wheat

topic: weed herbicide timing post-emergence days after sowing Phalaris minor
text: In north-western India, the main wheat weed Phalaris minor is controlled either with pre-emergence herbicides within 2 days of sowing or with post-emergence herbicides at about 30 days after sowing, and post-emergence use is by far the more common among farmers. Growth stage at spraying affects both weed control and crop tolerance. Product and dose must come from the KVK, and the label must be followed.
source_title: Spanish Journal of Agricultural Research: growth stages, weed control and herbicide tolerance in wheat (PAU, Ludhiana)
